PayPorter Local LLM – PDF Okuyucu Test Dokümanı
Bu doküman, PayPorter için geliştirilen yerel LLM/RAG sisteminin PDF okuma, metin
parçalama, anlamsal arama ve soru-cevap yeteneklerini test etmek amacıyla hazırlanmıştır.
İçerik gerçek bir yazılım geliştirme rehberi biçimindedir ve farklı başlıklar, kurallar, kod
örnekleri ve tablo içerir.
1. Okunabilir ve Anlaşılır Kod
Kod yalnızca bilgisayar tarafından çalıştırılmak için değil, insanlar tarafından okunmak için
de yazılır. Değişken, fonksiyon ve sınıf isimleri yaptıkları işi açıkça ifade etmelidir. x, a1 veya
tmp gibi belirsiz isimler yerine total_price, customer_id veya calculate_tax gibi açıklayıcı
isimler tercih edilmelidir.
2. İsimlendirme Kuralları
Projede kullanılan isimlendirme biçimi tutarlı olmalıdır. Python'da değişken ve fonksiyonlar
için snake_case, sınıflar için PascalCase yaygın olarak kullanılır. Sabit değerler büyük
harfle

tutarlı olmalıdır. Python'da değişken ve fonksiyonlar
için snake_case, sınıflar için PascalCase yaygın olarak kullanılır. Sabit değerler büyük
harflerle (MAX_RETRY_COUNT gibi) yazılabilir. Aynı projede farklı isimlendirme stillerinin
rastgele karıştırılması bakım maliyetini artırır.
3. Fonksiyonların Tek Sorumluluğu
Bir fonksiyon mümkün olduğunca tek bir işi yapmalıdır. Veri doğrulama, veritabanına kayıt
ve kullanıcıya mesaj üretme işlemlerinin tamamını tek fonksiyonda toplamak yerine
görevler küçük fonksiyonlara ayrılmalıdır. Bu yaklaşım test yazmayı ve hata ayıklamayı
kolaylaştırır.
Örnek:
 def calculate_total(price, tax_rate):
    tax = price * tax_rate
    return price + tax
4. DRY – Kendini Tekrar Etme
Aynı kod bloğu birden fazla yerde tekrar ediyorsa ortak bir fonksiyona veya modüle
taşınması düşünülmelidir. DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) prensibi, bir değişiklik gerektiğinde
aynı düzeltmenin birçok farklı noktada yapılmasını önler. Ancak gereksiz soyutlama da kodu
zorlaştırabilece

elf) prensibi, bir değişiklik gerektiğinde
aynı düzeltmenin birçok farklı noktada yapılmasını önler. Ancak gereksiz soyutlama da kodu
zorlaştırabileceği için denge korunmalıdır.
5. Hata Yönetimi
Uygulamalar hataların oluşabileceğini varsaymalıdır. Dosya okuma, ağ bağlantısı, kullanıcı
girdisi ve veritabanı işlemleri kontrollü şekilde ele alınmalıdır. Hataları sessizce yok saymak
yerine anlamlı log mesajları üretilmeli ve mümkünse kullanıcıya güvenli bir hata mesajı
gösterilmelidir.
6. Güvenlik Kuralları

Şifre, API anahtarı, token ve bağlantı bilgileri kaynak kod içine sabit olarak yazılmamalıdır.
Gizli bilgiler environment variable veya güvenli secret yönetim sistemlerinde tutulmalıdır.
Kullanıcı girdileri doğrulanmalı, yetkilendirme kontrolleri yalnızca arayüzde değil sunucu
tarafında da uygulanmalıdır. SQL sorgularında parametreli sorgular kullanmak SQL injection
riskini azaltır.
7. Loglama
Loglar sistem davranışını anlamak ve sorunları incelemek için önemlidir. INFO seviyesinde
normal iş akışı, WARNING seviyesinde beklenmeyen fakat sistemi durdurmayan durumlar,
ERROR seviyesinde ise başarısız işlemler kaydedilebilir. Şifre, kart bilgisi, erişim tokenı veya
kişisel hassas veriler loglara açık biçimde yazılmamalıdır.
8. Yorum Satırları ve Dokümantasyon
Yorumlar kodun ne yaptığını tekrar etmek yerine neden o şekilde yazıldığını açıklamalıdır.
Karmaşık iş kuralları, beklenmeyen teknik kararlar ve fonksiyonların giriş/çıkış davranışları
belgel

yerine neden o şekilde yazıldığını açıklamalıdır.
Karmaşık iş kuralları, beklenmeyen teknik kararlar ve fonksiyonların giriş/çıkış davranışları
belgelenmelidir. Güncelliğini kaybetmiş yorumlar yanlış yönlendirebileceği için kod
değiştiğinde dokümantasyon da güncellenmelidir.
9. Git ve Versiyon Kontrolü
Değişiklikler küçük ve anlamlı commit'lere bölünmelidir. Commit mesajı yapılan değişikliği
açıklamalıdır. Örneğin 'fix' yerine 'Fix PDF text extraction for empty pages' daha faydalıdır.
Ana branch üzerinde doğrudan riskli geliştirmeler yapmak yerine feature branch
kullanılması önerilir.
10. Test Yazımı
Kritik fonksiyonlar için otomatik testler oluşturulmalıdır. Normal kullanım senaryolarının
yanında boş değer, yanlış veri tipi, sınır değer ve hata senaryoları da test edilmelidir. Bir test
başarısız olduğunda hangi davranışın bozulduğu kolayca anlaşılabilmelidir.
11. Performans
Önce doğru ve okunabilir kod yazılmalı, ardından ölçüm yapılarak gerçek darboğazlar
optimize edilmelidir. Gereks

ca anlaşılabilmelidir.
11. Performans
Önce doğru ve okunabilir kod yazılmalı, ardından ölçüm yapılarak gerçek darboğazlar
optimize edilmelidir. Gereksiz dosya okuma, tekrarlanan veritabanı sorguları ve büyük veri
kümelerinin belleğe tamamen alınması performans sorunlarına yol açabilir.
12. Kod İnceleme Kontrol Listesi
Kod incelemesinde şu sorular sorulabilir: Kod anlaşılır mı? İsimler açıklayıcı mı? Tekrarlanan
kod var mı? Hata durumları ele alınmış mı? Hassas bilgi açığa çıkıyor mu? Fonksiyon
gereğinden uzun mu? Test edilebilir mi? Log mesajları yeterli mi? Değişiklik mevcut
davranışları bozabilir mi?

 Account Provisioning, Role Changes, Temporary Access and Offboarding
Test Document: Bu doküman PayPorter Local LLM / RAG sisteminin çoklu PDF arama, chunk

PayPorter iç politikası değildir.
1. Purpose
This policy defines a consistent process for creating, changing, reviewing and removing
employee access to PayPorter systems. The goal is to ensure that users receive the access
required for their responsibilities without maintaining unnecessary permissions.
2. Scope
The policy applies to employees, interns, contractors and other authorized users who require
access to PayPorter applications, internal systems, development environments, shared
resources or administrative tools.
3. New Employee Onboarding
Access provisioning should begin only after an approved onbo

opment environments, shared
resources or administrative tools.
3. New Employee Onboarding
Access provisioning should begin only after an approved onboarding request is received. The
request should identify the user's department, manager, job role, start date and required
systems. Accounts should not be created solely on the basis of an informal chat message when
an approved workflow is required.
4. Unique User Accounts
Each user should receive an individual account. Shared user accounts should be avoided
unless a documented technical or business requirement makes them necessary. Individual
accounts improve accountability because system actions can be associated with a specific
authorized user.
5. Initial Passwords
Temporary or initial passwords must be delivered through an approved method. Users should
be required to change temporary credentials when appropriate. Initial passwords must not be
posted in public channels or stored in openly accessible documents.
6. Role-Based Access
Acces

entials when appropriate. Initial passwords must not be
posted in public channels or stored in openly accessible documents.
6. Role-Based Access
Access should be assigned according to the user's role and responsibilities. A developer,
finance employee, support specialist and system administrator may require different
permissions. Users should not automatically receive access simply because another person in
the organization has it.
7. Least Privilege
Users must receive only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their assigned work.
Administrative privileges should be granted separately and only when justified. Convenience
alone is not sufficient reason to provide permanent elevated access.
8. Manager Approval

Access to sensitive applications, production systems or privileged administrative functions
should require appropriate approval. The responsible manager or system owner should
confirm that the requested access is necessary for the user's role.
9. Temporary Access
Temporary elevated access should have a defined purpose and expiration period. For this test
policy, temporary privileged access should normally expire within 24 hours unless a longer
period is explicitly approved. Expired access should be removed automatically where
technically possible.
10. Department or Role Changes
When an employee changes department or job responsibilities, existing access should be
reviewed instead of simply adding new permissions. Permissions that are no longer required
must be removed to prevent privilege accumulation over time.
11. Access Reviews
Sensitive and privileged access should be reviewed periodically. For this test pol

ved to prevent privilege accumulation over time.
11. Access Reviews
Sensitive and privileged access should be reviewed periodically. For this test policy, privileged
access reviews should occur at least every three months. Reviewers should verify that the user
is still active, the permission remains necessary and the assigned access level is appropriate.
12. Intern and Contractor Accounts
Intern and contractor accounts should have a documented sponsor or responsible manager
and, where possible, a predefined expiration date. Their access should be limited to the
systems necessary for the assigned work. Extensions should require review rather than
occurring automatically.
13. Production Access
Production access should be more restrictive than access to development or test
environments. Direct production access should only be granted when required by the user's
responsibilities. High-risk production changes should follow the organization's approved
change and review process.

quired by the user's
responsibilities. High-risk production changes should follow the organization's approved
change and review process.
14. Service Accounts
Service accounts should be used for applications or automated processes rather than normal
interactive employee activity. Service account credentials must be protected, ownership must
be documented and unused service accounts should be disabled or removed.
15. Account Inactivity
Inactive accounts may represent unnecessary security risk. Accounts that have not been used
for an extended period should be reviewed. If the account is no longer required, it should be
disabled according to the applicable operational procedure.
16. Employee Offboarding
When employment or an authorized engagement ends, access must be removed promptly
according to the offboarding process. High-risk or privileged access should receive particular
attention. Active sessions, remote access permissions, application accounts and administrative
privileges should b

ed access should receive particular
attention. Active sessions, remote access permissions, application accounts and administrative
privileges should be considered.
17. Company Assets

Company laptops, access cards, hardware tokens and other assigned assets should be
returned according to the offboarding process. Loss of an authentication device or company
asset should be reported immediately so that associated access can be reviewed or revoked.
18. Access Logging
Important account lifecycle events such as account creation, privileged access assignment,
role changes and account disabling should be logged where supported. Logs should allow
authorized teams to investigate when access was granted or removed and who approved
significant changes.
19. Emergency Access
Emergency administrative access may be used when normal access processes cannot support
an urgent critical incident. Emergency access must be limited, monitored and reviewed after
use. Emergency procedures must not become a routine method for bypassing normal approval
requirements.
20. Policy Exceptions

20. Policy Exceptions
Exceptions require a documented business reason and appropriate approval. An exception
should identify the affected system, user, requested permission, duration and any additional
controls required to reduce risk.

PayPorter – Data Backup & Disaster Recovery | Test Document
Page 1
 PayPorter Data Backup & Disaster
 Recovery Policy
 Backup, Restore, Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
Test Document: Bu belge PayPorter Local LLM / RAG sisteminde PDF okuma, chunking,
semantic retrieval ve soru-cevap testleri için hazırlanmış örnek bir kurumsal politika
dokümanıdır. Gerçek şirket politikası değildir.
1. Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to define minimum requirements for protecting PayPorter data
through reliable backups and for restoring critical systems following data loss, infrastructure
failure, cybersecurity incidents or other disruptive events.
2. Scope
This policy applies to critical application data, databases, configuration files, business
documents, system configurations and other information assets identified as necessary for
business operations. Systems should be classified according to their operational importance
and recovery requirements.
3. Backup Frequency
Critical producti

ss operations. Systems should be classified according to their operational importance
and recovery requirements.
3. Backup Frequency
Critical production databases should be backed up at least once every 24 hours unless a
system-specific requirement defines a shorter interval. Highly dynamic or transaction-sensitive
systems may require more frequent backups. Backup schedules must be documented and
monitored for failed jobs.
4. Backup Types
Backup strategies may include full, incremental and differential backups. A full backup
contains the selected dataset at a specific point in time. Incremental backups store changes
since the previous backup, while differential backups store changes since the most recent full
backup. The selected method should balance recovery speed, storage requirements and
operational risk.
5. Backup Retention
Backup copies must be retained according to business, legal and technical requirements. For
this test policy, daily backups are retained for 30 days, weekly ba

pies must be retained according to business, legal and technical requirements. For
this test policy, daily backups are retained for 30 days, weekly backups for 12 weeks and
monthly backups for 12 months. Retention periods may be extended when required by an
approved business or compliance need.
6. Backup Storage and Separation
At least one backup copy for critical systems should be logically or physically separated from
the primary production environment. A failure, ransomware event or administrative mistake
affecting the production system should not automatically destroy every available backup copy.
7. Encryption
Backups containing confidential, personal or financial information should be encrypted using
approved methods. Encryption keys must be protected separately from the backup data and
access should be limited to authorized personnel.

PayPorter – Data Backup & Disaster Recovery | Test Document
Page 2
8. Access Control
Access to backup repositories, recovery consoles and administrative restore functions must
follow the least privilege principle. Backup deletion permissions should be especially restricted
because an attacker with deletion access could interfere with recovery after an incident.
9. Backup Monitoring
Backup jobs must be monitored for completion and failure. A successful job status alone
should not be treated as proof that the data is recoverable. Repeated failures, unusual backup
size changes or missing backup sets should be investigated.
10. Restore Testing
Critical backups must be tested through periodic restoration exercises. For this test policy,
critical systems should undergo a restore test at least once every three months. The test
should confirm that data can be recovered, that the recovered information is usable and that
the recovery procedure is documented.
11. Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
Re

t data can be recovered, that the recovered information is usable and that
the recovery procedure is documented.
11. Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
Recovery Point Objective defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in
time. For example, an RPO of four hours means the recovery design should aim to restore data
to a point no more than four hours before the disruption. Different systems may have different
RPO values.
12. Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
Recovery Time Objective defines the target time for restoring a service after a disruption. For
example, an RTO of two hours means the organization aims to return the relevant service to
an acceptable operational state within two hours. RTO and RPO describe different recovery
requirements and should not be confused.
13. Disaster Declaration
A disaster recovery process may be activated when a critical service cannot be restored
through normal incident procedures within an acceptable period, when primary infrastructure
becomes

tivated when a critical service cannot be restored
through normal incident procedures within an acceptable period, when primary infrastructure
becomes unavailable or when a major cybersecurity event requires systems to be rebuilt in a
controlled recovery environment.
14. Recovery Priority
Recovery activities should follow documented business priorities. Identity and authentication
services, network connectivity, critical databases and core transaction services may be
restored before lower-priority supporting systems when dependencies require this order.
15. Cybersecurity and Ransomware Recovery
Following a ransomware or suspected compromise event, systems should not automatically be
restored into an environment that may still be compromised. The incident should first be
contained and recovery sources should be assessed for integrity. Known-clean backups should
be preferred for restoration.
16. Recovery Documentation
Recovery procedures should identify responsible roles, required creden

n-clean backups should
be preferred for restoration.
16. Recovery Documentation
Recovery procedures should identify responsible roles, required credentials, dependencies,
backup locations and validation steps. Documentation must be maintained so that recovery
does not depend entirely on the memory of a single employee.

17. Roles and Responsibilities
System owners are responsible for defining business recovery requirements. Technical teams
are responsible for implementing backup and recovery mechanisms. Security teams may
support integrity checks and incident response, while authorized management determines
business priorities during major disruptions.
18. Review and Improvement
Backup and disaster recovery procedures should be reviewed after significant infrastructure
changes, major incidents or failed recovery tests. Lessons learned should be used to update
technical procedures, recovery priorities and monitoring controls.

1. Amaç ve Kapsam
Bu politikanın amacı; şirket bilgilerini, kullanıcı verilerini, yazılım sistemlerini ve erişim
bilgilerini yetkisiz erişim, değiştirme, ifşa, kayıp ve kötüye kullanıma karşı korumaktır. Politika
çalışanları, stajyerleri, yüklenicileri, uygulamaları, sunucuları, istemci cihazlarını ve şirket
tarafından kullanılan bulut veya yerel sistemleri kapsar.
2. Erişim Kontrolü
Sistem erişimleri en az ayrıcalık (least privilege) prensibine göre verilmelidir. Kullanıcı yalnızca
görevi için gerekli kaynaklara erişebilmelidir. Yönetici yetkileri standart kullanıcı hesaplarından
ayrılmalı, işten ayrılan v

dir. Kullanıcı yalnızca
görevi için gerekli kaynaklara erişebilmelidir. Yönetici yetkileri standart kullanıcı hesaplarından
ayrılmalı, işten ayrılan veya görevi değişen kişilerin erişimleri zamanında gözden geçirilmeli ve
kaldırılmalıdır.
3. Kimlik Doğrulama ve Parola Güvenliği
Kullanıcı hesaplarında güçlü ve benzersiz parolalar kullanılmalıdır. Parolalar başka kullanıcılarla
paylaşılmamalı veya düz metin dosyalarda saklanmamalıdır. Kritik sistemlerde mümkün
olduğunda çok faktörlü kimlik doğrulama (MFA) kullanılmalıdır. Varsayılan parolalar sistem
devreye alınmadan önce değiştirilmelidir.
4. API Anahtarları ve Gizli Bilgiler
API key, access token, private key, veritabanı parolası ve benzeri gizli bilgiler kaynak kod içine
hard-code edilmemelidir. Bu değerler environment variable, secret manager veya kurumun
onayladığı güvenli bir yapı üzerinden yönetilmelidir. Gizli bilgiler Git repository, log dosyası
veya ekran görüntüsü üzerinden paylaşılmamalıdır.
5. Veri Koruma
Hassas veriler yaln

rinden yönetilmelidir. Gizli bilgiler Git repository, log dosyası
veya ekran görüntüsü üzerinden paylaşılmamalıdır.
5. Veri Koruma
Hassas veriler yalnızca iş amacı için gerekli olduğu ölçüde işlenmelidir. Veriler aktarım
sırasında ve gerektiğinde depolama sırasında uygun şifreleme yöntemleriyle korunmalıdır.
Kişisel veya finansal bilgiler yetkisiz kişilerle paylaşılmamalı; test ortamlarında gerçek müşteri

1. Purpose
This policy defines the minimum security requirements for employees, contractors and
authorized third parties who access PayPorter systems remotely. The objective is to reduce
risks related to unauthorized access, insecure networks, lost devices, credential theft and
improper use of corporate resources.
2. Scope
The policy applies to all users who connect to PayPorter systems from outside an approved
corporate network. It covers company laptops, approved personal devices, VPN connections,
remote desktop sessions, cloud services, internal applications and other systems that require
remote authentic

remote desktop sessions, cloud services, internal applications and other systems that require
remote authentication.
3. Authorized Remote Access
Remote access to PayPorter resources must be authorized according to the user's business
role. Users must only access systems required for their assigned responsibilities. Access rights
should follow the least privilege principle and must be reviewed when a user's role changes or
employment ends.
4. VPN Requirement
When access to an internal PayPorter resource requires a secure corporate connection, users
must connect through the approved company VPN. Users must not attempt to bypass the VPN
requirement by using unauthorized tunneling tools, proxy services or alternative remote
access software. VPN credentials are personal and must never be shared with another person.
5. Multi-Factor Authentication
Where supported, remote access and VPN authentication should use multi-factor
authentication (MFA). A passw

5. Multi-Factor Authentication
Where supported, remote access and VPN authentication should use multi-factor
authentication (MFA). A password alone should not be considered sufficient protection for
high-risk or privileged remote access. Users must not approve an MFA request that they did
not initiate.
6. Password and Credential Security
Passwords must be strong, unique and protected from unauthorized disclosure. Corporate
passwords must not be reused for unrelated personal services. Passwords, VPN credentials,
access tokens and recovery codes must not be stored in plain text notes, source code, chat
messages or publicly accessible documents.
7. Device Security Requirements
Devices used for remote work must have supported operating systems, current security
updates and an active screen lock. Company-managed security software must not be disabled.
Users should lock the device when leaving it unattended and should report a lost or stolen
corporate device as soon as possible.

8. Public and Untrusted Networks
Public Wi-Fi networks may expose traffic to additional risks. Users should avoid sensitive work
on unknown or untrusted networks whenever possible. When remote access is necessary, the
approved VPN should be used before accessing protected corporate resources. Users must not
disable security controls merely to make a public network connection work.
9. Home Network Security
Employees working from home should use a password-protected wireless network. Default
router administrator passwords should be changed when possible, and modern wireless
security settings should be used. Corporate devices should not be intentionally exposed
directly to the public internet.
10. Remote Desktop and Administrative Access
Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), SSH and other administrative services must only be exposed
when there is a legitimate business requirement and appropriate security controls are in place.

Administrative access should be restricted to authorized users and, where applicable,
reachable only through VPN or another approved secure access method.
11. File Transfer and Local Storage
Confidential PayPorter information should only be transferred through approved services.
Users should avoid copying sensitive company data to unmanaged personal devices, personal
cloud storage or removable media. Files downloaded for legitimate remote work should be
deleted from temporary locations when they are no longer required.
12. Email, Phishing and Social Engineering
Remote workers must remain alert to phishing attempts requesting passwords, VPN
credentials, MFA approvals or urgent file downloads. Unexpected login pages and
authentication requests should be verified before credentials are entered. Suspicious
messages should be reported through the appro

ed login pages and
authentication requests should be verified before credentials are entered. Suspicious
messages should be reported through the approved security or IT reporting process.
13. Logging and Monitoring
Remote access systems may record authentication events, connection times, source
information, failed login attempts and security-relevant activity for operational and security
purposes. Logs must be protected against unauthorized modification and should not
unnecessarily contain passwords, tokens or other secret values.
14. Split Tunneling
Split tunneling must follow PayPorter's approved VPN configuration. Users must not manually
change VPN routing or split-tunneling settings to bypass corporate security controls. Any
exception must be reviewed and approved by the responsible technical or security team.
15. Software Installation
Users must not install unauthorized remote access, VPN, proxy or network tunneling software
on company-managed devices. Software required for busine

Users must not install unauthorized remote access, VPN, proxy or network tunneling software
on company-managed devices. Software required for business purposes should be obtained
through an approved source and should be kept up to date.
16. Security Incident Reporting
Users must promptly report suspected credential theft, unusual MFA requests, unexpected
VPN sessions, lost devices, malware alerts or unauthorized access. If compromise is suspected,

17. VPN Session Termination
VPN sessions should be disconnected when secure remote access is no longer required.
Long-running, unattended or suspicious sessions may be terminated by authorized
administrators. Users should sign out of corporate applications when completing work on
shared or temporary environments.
18. Policy Exceptions
Any exception to this policy must have a documented business justification and appropriate
approval. Exceptions should be limited in scope and duration, and compensating security
controls should be applied where necessary.
